bot_token.help: Bot API token issued by @BotFather on Telegram. Format: <bot_id>:<token>. Stored encrypted at rest.

parse_mode.help: Optional. Markdown or HTML to enable rich formatting in Title + Message. Leave blank for plain text. The host does not pre-escape special characters — switch to plain text if your messages contain Telegram-reserved characters.

disable_notification.help: Optional. When true, sends the message without a notification sound on the recipient device. Useful for low-priority alerts.

page.title: Telegrams
page.subtitle: Route workflow, alert, and backup events to a Telegram chat via the Bot API. The plugin handles Test (getMe liveness) and Send (sendMessage) — there is no OAuth flow because bots use a long-lived bearer token.
page.registerHint: Add a channel from the host's Notifications > Channels page and pick "Telegram" as the channel_type.

help.name: How this channel appears in McHarbor lists and alert rules.

help.chatId: Recipient chat identifier: numeric user/group ID or @channelname. Use getUpdates to discover a chat_id for private chats.
help.parseMode: Markdown or HTML enables rich formatting in Title + Message. Plain text passes characters through verbatim.
help.disableNotification: When on, sends without a notification sound on the recipient device. Useful for low-priority alerts.

guide.title: Telegram setup guide
guide.step1: Open Telegram and start a chat with @BotFather. Send /newbot and follow the prompts (display name + unique username ending in "bot"). BotFather replies with the bot token in the format :. Paste that into the Bot Token field on the left.
guide.step2: Start a chat with your bot (search for the @username you just created) and send any message. The bot needs at least one inbound message before it can post to that chat — Telegram blocks bot-initiated contact until the user speaks first.
guide.step3: For a private chat, get the chat_id by calling https://api.telegram.org/bot/getUpdates after step 2 — the response includes "chat":{"id": }. For a public channel, use @channelname (the @ is part of the identifier).
guide.step4: For groups: add the bot as a member, then promote it to Post Messages in the group permissions. Without that right sendMessage returns 403 Forbidden.
guide.step5: For channels: add the bot as an administrator with Post Messages permission. Plain members cannot post; the bot must be an admin.
guide.step6: Paste the chat_id (or @channelname) into the Chat ID field on the left. Leave Parse Mode blank unless your messages will only contain Telegram-safe formatting. Toggle Silent Send on for low-priority backup-completion alerts.
guide.step7: Click Save and test connection. The plugin issues a getMe against the Bot API to confirm the token is live. The host does NOT send a test message — getMe just echoes the bot identity. If getMe returns 401, double-check the bot token.
guide.step8: Once the channel is saved, route workflow or alert events to it from Settings > Notifications > Rules. Telegram delivery is fire-and-forget: a failed send is logged in the audit log and surfaced in the host toast, but the host does not retry.
